newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane falls, but finds floor on demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane falls, but finds floor on demand.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices tracked weakening NYMEX futures in moderate midday trade on Wednesday, but quickly found a floor with the help of cold weather and crop drying demand in the Midwest, players said.
Snow and winds bringing below freezing temperatures were expected in the Midwest later Wednesday or Thursday, which could drive up the demand for propane as a home heating fuel in the hub.
In addition, less than 50 percent of the U.S. corn crop has been harvested and what is still out in the fields is very wet, said traders.
"Liftings for propane are still good," said one Midwest trader.
In the Conway, Kansas, hub, spot November propane traded at 54.50 cents -- about 1.25 cents below Tuesday levels -- after falling lower at the open.
"Conway tried to sell of but the buyers came back in," said a trader.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane fell one cent to between 53.25 cents and 53.50 cents a gallon in moderate activity.
Belvieu hub was taken down by NYMEX December crude oil futures, which started to sell off following Tuesday's night bearish API stock data.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
